title: A message on the machine
text: …signal. Low battery. Year reads 1983. That can't be right. Your answering machine is blinking.

title: The first install
text: Someone wants a line. Everything you need is on the van. Outside wall first, then indoors.

title: The switchboard
text: Their socket is in. The line is still dead until you jumper it at the switchboard in your room.

title: Odd jobs
text: One subscriber won't cover the rent. A neighbour has something that needs fixing.

title: Door to door
text: Customers won't all ring you. Knock on a door.

title: The round
text: You know the round now. The phone will ring by itself. When you can afford help, the notebook has the page.

title: The farm line
text: Ruth Adeyemi has asked politely twice. No fee buys a line out there. You'll have to build it.

title: Behind Main Street
text: The farm has dial tone and the whole town heard who built it. Behind Main Street, Church Lane has never had a phone that worked on a Sunday. Father Roe says the Lord can wait. The parish council can't.

title: The valley road
text: Eastgate is a short drive down the valley road. NezTel calls it 'scheduled for the next phase'. The Post Office has been in the next phase since 1971.

title: Ninety-nine percent
text: NezTel's leaflet promises 99%. Doc Ferreira did the sum on the back of it: three and a half days a year with no line. Do better than that and people notice. Fix faults the day they show, and don't keep anyone waiting.

title: The valley is yours
text: Two villages, one switchboard, and service NezTel can't match. PIP's Almanac has a page about modems answering in turn, and a word underlined three times: web.

title: The road out is NezTel's
text: The web is out there and the only road to it is NezTel's trunk. Lease it, because you have to. Then build your own way out over the ridge, because you can.

title: The boom
text: Everybody wants a web page and somewhere to keep it. Millbrook over the hills, a cold store in Eastgate, and across the water, Farland. NezTel owns the only ocean cable. For now.

title: Always on
text: Nobody wants to hear a modem shriek any more. Broadband over the copper, a ring of fibre round the bay, and Farland's capital, where NezTel charges twice what you do.

title: The Core
text: Your network is a modem bank behind a shop, a cabinet that floods, servers in a fish store and two long cables, and you built every bit of it in a hurry. Everything should go through one building. Halden Flats is empty, flat and boring, and every cable you own already passes it.

title: In everyone's pocket
text: The phone doesn't need a wall any more. Masts on the ridge, masts along the coast, and fibre behind every one. PIP has started finishing your sentences, which is new.
